correctness.rationale: Cut-edge contraction yields a tree of bridge-free components. When attaching a fresh graph H at c in old A to vertex a in H, all new square edges connect a to N_A[c] and each neighbor of a to c; both closed neighborhoods are cliques. For q large, a has q-deg_A(c)-1 colors; among H^2 colorings fixing a, fraction (q-1-deg_H(a))/(q-1) avoid old c color on its neighbors. This gives exact factor P_H(q)*(q-deg_A(c)-1)*(q-deg_H(a)-1)/(q(q-1)); products telescope into falling factorials with bridge counts, yielding a polynomial identity by infinitely many q. Chromatic number follows from positivity thresholds and singleton case. Independently enumerated exact named-color counts for all connected labelled graphs n<=5, palettes q=2,3,4: 2,316 agreements; finite tests only corroborate general induction.
